nodes.name: Hydrous Nickel Oxide Growth via RPSM
nodes.procedure: Prior to each experiment the surface of the working electrode was polished with 1200 grit carbimet paper, dipped in H₂SO₄, wiped, and polished with a slurry of 0.3 micron alumina powder until a 'mirror bright' finish was achieved. Before commencing each experiment, nitrogen gas was bubbled through the electrolyte solution for 20 min. The polymeric Ni oxy-hydroxide films were prepared via multi-cycling the Ni electrode between the switching potentials of -1.450 V and 0.65 V (vs Hg/HgO) at a scan rate of 0.15 V s⁻¹ in aqueous NaOH solutions (0.1-5.0 mol dm⁻³). Films of different thicknesses were prepared by varying the number of growth cycles N. The charge storage capacity Q follows Q = 0.0014(1-exp[-0.045N]) C.

nodes.description: Redox switching dynamics analysis via cyclic voltammetry

working_electrode.value: polycrystalline nickel foil with hydrous oxide film

charge_capacity_increase.unit: at low sweep rates for thick films

nodes.source_text: The dynamics of redox switching has been quantified in terms of a diffusive frequency using the Laviron-Aoki diffusion model... The diffusive frequency decreases smoothly with increasing number of oxide growth cycles N from a value close to 1.0 s^{-1} for the thinnest nickel oxyhydroxide films to ca. 0.2 s^{-1} for layers formed after ca. 360 cycles.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV shows characteristic Ni(II/III) redox peaks in 0.40-0.50 V vs Hg/HgO region that develop with cycling; thin films (N=30) show A2 at 0.48 V, A2' shoulder at 0.54 V; thick films (N=120) show single A2 at 0.50 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The growth of the film is evident from the set of redox peaks located in the potential region 0.40 − 0.50 V vs. Hg/HgO which become increasingly more developed with increasing number of potential cycles.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV charge capacity Q follows Q = 0.0014(1-exp[-0.045N]) C where N is growth cycles; peak width ΔEp/2 ≈ 45 mV at low sweep rates, increases to >90 mV at high rates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The oxide growth kinetics can be fit to the following empirical expression: Q = a(1−exp[−bN]) where a = 0.0014±7.43×10⁻⁵ C and b = 0.045±0.0004 cycle⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffusive frequency τ_D = D/L² decreases from ~1.0 s⁻¹ for thin films to ~0.2 s⁻¹ for thick films (N=360 cycles), determined via Laviron-Aoki analysis of sweep rate dependence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffusive frequency decreases smoothly with increasing number of oxide growth cycles N from a value close to 1.0 s⁻¹ for the thinnest nickel oxyhydroxide films to ca. 0.2 s⁻¹ for layers formed after ca. 360 cycles.

nodes.characterization_summary: LSV Tafel analysis gives ~60 mV/dec low overpotential slope, ~120 mV/dec high overpotential slope; reaction order m_OH⁻ ≈ 1.0 invariant across potential regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Steady state Tafel plot analysis has been used to elucidate the kinetics and mechanism of oxygen evolution with slopes of ca. 60 mV dec⁻¹ and ca. 120 mV dec⁻¹ at low and high overpotentials respectively, whereas the reaction order with respect to hydroxide ion activity remains invariant at ca. 1.0...

nodes.characterization_summary: CV redox peaks exhibit super-Nernstian pH dependence dE/dpH = -88 mV/pH for hydrous A2/C2 peaks vs Nernstian for anhydrous peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the anhydrous A₂′/C₂′ peaks exhibit a regular Nernstian shift whereas the hydrous counterparts A₂/C₂ exhibit ... a supernernstian potential-pH shift, which typically has the value of dE/dpH = −2.303(3RT/2F) = −0.088 V/pH unit at T = 298 K.
